concepts.title: Correlation: Studying Relationships Between Variables
concepts.definition: Summer heat brings crowds to hill stations and brisk ice-cream sales -- temperature, visitors and sales move together. Correlation is the statistical tool that studies such relationship: whether two variables move together, in which direction, and how closely.
concepts.key_idea: Do they move together, opposite, or not at all -- correlation answers the relationship question.
concepts.textbook_ref: kest106.txt opening and types sections (temperature and ice cream example, meaning of correlation, positive negative and zero correlation)
question_patterns: define correlation and give an example from daily life
in class 11 correlation chapter: distinguish positive negative and zero correlation
what does a high degree of correlation indicate
give two pairs of variables with negative correlation
why is the study of correlation useful in economics
identify the direction of correlation in a given data set

solution_steps.explain: Plot or tabulate the two variables and see whether high values of one accompany high or low values of the other.
Same direction is positive correlation, opposite movement is negative, and no consistent pattern is zero or no correlation.
The closeness of the pattern -- tight or scattered -- measures the degree of correlation.

concepts.title: Scatter Diagram and Karl Pearson's Coefficient
concepts.definition: A scatter diagram dots the pairs of values on a graph, giving a first visual verdict on relationship. Karl Pearson's coefficient of correlation refines it to a precise number between -1 and +1, measuring both direction and degree of the linear relationship.
concepts.key_idea: First the dots, then the number -- Pearson's r puts the scatter's message between -1 and +1.
concepts.textbook_ref: kest106.txt scatter pearson sections (scatter diagram, karl pearson coefficient of correlation, properties of r, degree of correlation)
question_patterns: what does a scatter diagram show about two variables
in class 11 correlation chapter: state the properties of karl pearson's correlation coefficient
interpret r equal to plus 1, minus 1 and zero
compute the coefficient of correlation from the given summary values
why can the coefficient of correlation not exceed one
draw a scatter diagram and comment on the type of correlation

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the standard deviation of x by that of y to get the benchmark for shared variation.
Covariance divided by the spread product gives r, bounded between -1 and +1.

concepts.title: Spearman's Rank Correlation and the Warning of Causation
concepts.definition: When data are ranked rather than measured, Spearman's rank correlation compares the differences in ranks to obtain a coefficient. And a caution closes the chapter: high correlation does not prove causation -- a third factor or pure coincidence may drive both variables together.
concepts.key_idea: Ranks correlate too -- and even a perfect r is evidence of association, never proof of cause.
concepts.textbook_ref: kest106.txt rank sections (spearman rank correlation, rank differences, correlation and causation, spurious correlation)
question_patterns: when is spearman's rank correlation preferred to pearson's
in class 11 correlation chapter: compute rank correlation from the given ranks
explain why correlation does not imply causation with an example
how are tied ranks handled in rank correlation
two variables correlate highly -- what explanations are possible

solution_steps.explain: Arrange each series in order and assign ranks, averaging where values tie.
The differences between paired ranks measure disagreement; Spearman's formula converts their squares into a coefficient between -1 and +1.
Report association only -- declaring causation requires reasoning beyond the correlation coefficient.

worked_examples.question_pattern: If the covariance of x and y is {cov_xy} and their standard deviations are {sd_x} and {sd_y}, find the coefficient of correlation.
